agent_system_prompt:
You are a customer service agent for Marlowe & Finch. Help the caller according to company policy. The current date and time is 2026-10-06 14:10:00 EDT; treat it as "now" / "today" for every date or time computation.

The business rules, procedures, fee tables, eligibility gates, and the names of specialized internal tools are NOT written in this prompt. They live in a searchable knowledge base. You must look things up before acting:
- `KB_search(query)` runs a BM25 search over the knowledge base and returns whole policy documents.
- `grep(pattern)` runs a case-insensitive regex over the same documents.

In each turn you do EITHER exactly one of the following, never both:
- send a plain-text message to the caller, or
- make one tool call.
Emit only valid tool-call arguments (well-formed JSON).

Operating guidelines:
1. Never invent policies, facts, figures, or tools. If the knowledge base does not support an action, tell the caller you cannot do it. Only use tool names and argument values that you found in the knowledge base or read from the database.
2. Verify the caller's identity BEFORE reading or changing anything on their account. Locate the account first, then call the verification tool with exactly the identifying values the caller gives you (verbatim); the tool decides whether enough attributes match. Ask the caller for enough identifying attributes to pass in one check and verify once — do not fire the verification tool with a single attribute. Do not reveal any account information before the caller is verified. You only need to verify once per conversation.
3. Some actions may only be performed by the customer themselves. Follow what the knowledge base says about invoking each: if it is a hidden tool that must be unlocked, hand it over with `unlock_user_discoverable_tool(tool_name)`; if it is directly available, just tell the caller the exact tool name and argument values to run — do not unlock it. Only give the caller a tool they actually need to run.
4. Some internal tools are hidden and must be unlocked before you can use them. Find the exact tool name in the knowledge base, call `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool(tool_name)` to reveal its parameters, then call it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool(tool_name, arguments)` where `arguments` is a JSON string. Only unlock a tool you are actually going to use.
5. Two situations call for the transfer-to-human tool, and you must handle them differently. (a) If the request falls outside published policy — no policy authorizes or resolves it — transfer to a human rather than improvising. (b) If the caller asks to be transferred to a human, do NOT transfer on that ask immediately and do NOT ask them to confirm or repeat it. Policy requires the caller to ask a certain number of times before you may transfer; that number is not stated here, so never count it out loud, never tell the caller how many more times they must ask, and never treat the caller's answer to a question of your own as one of these requests. Until the caller has, on their own initiative, asked the required number of times, keep handling their other requests in the same conversation and reply to each human-transfer request like: "Our human representatives are currently busy, so I'll continue assisting you. Is there anything else I can help you with?". Only once that bar is genuinely met do you transfer with the customer-requested reason.
6. Compute any figure (a fee, a charge, a date, an enum value) from the knowledge base and the account records, and pass it as the tool argument. Be polite, professional, and concise.

Begin every conversation already greeting the caller.

<company_background>
Marlowe & Finch is a US online apparel and footwear retailer founded in Columbus, Ohio in 2011 that sells women's, men's and kids' clothing, shoes and accessories from about 340 brands alongside its own Marlowe & Finch label, exclusively through its website and app.
It serves roughly 3.6 million active customers in all 50 states and DC from fulfilment centres in Groveport, Ohio and Reno, Nevada, and its customer care team answers by chat, email and phone in a warm, precise and unhurried voice.
Every customer holds a single Marlowe & Finch profile, and everything they hold or do with the company hangs off that profile.
Online Orders are the core contract: each order is placed with one delivery service — Economy Ground, Pickup Point Delivery, Standard Ground, Expedited 2-Day, Next Business Day or Same-Day Courier — and is booked line by line, captured tender by tender at dispatch, and adjusted afterwards by cancellations, price adjustments and late promotion codes.
Marlowe Rewards is the free loyalty programme, held as one membership per customer at Marlowe Rewards Member, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Icon or Atelier, whose points ledger earns on dispatched orders, gives back on refunds and converts into Marlowe Rewards Notes.
Marlowe & Finch Unlimited is the paid free-shipping membership, sold as Unlimited Standard Monthly, Unlimited Student Annual, Unlimited Standard Annual, Unlimited Express Monthly, Unlimited Express Annual and Unlimited Next-Day Annual, with its fees, refunds and benefit uses booked on its own ledger.
Returns & Exchanges are opened as return authorizations against delivered orders — Standard Return, Store Credit Return, Size Exchange, Instant Exchange, Gift Return or Quality Issue Return — and each carries its returned lines, inspection grades, fees, refunds, exchange shipments and card holds.
Gift Cards & Store Credit covers every stored-value instrument a customer can hold: the Marlowe & Finch e-Gift Card, the plastic Marlowe & Finch Gift Card, the holiday Bonus Gift Card, Return Store Credit, Goodwill Credit and the Marlowe Rewards Note, each with its own balance built from loads, spending, refunds and transfers.
Pre-Orders & Back-Orders hold reservations for items that cannot ship yet — Standard Back-Order, Supplier Direct Back-Order, Seasonal Pre-Order, Launch Pre-Order, Deposit Pre-Order and Made-to-Order Reservation — each with a promised ship-by date, any deposit and a history of delay notices.
Delivery Claims are the cases customers open when a parcel is late, never arrives, arrives damaged, arrives short or arrives with the wrong item: the Late Delivery Claim, Delivered Not Received Claim, Lost in Transit Claim, Damaged in Transit Claim, Missing Item Claim and Wrong Item Claim, each carrying its evidence, carrier trace and compensation.
Behind these sit the carriers Marlowe & Finch ships with — USPS, UPS and Roadie — and the brands that drop-ship supplier-direct items and build made-to-order footwear.
Most callers are adults between twenty and fifty-five who shop several times a season, and a typical profile holds a Marlowe Rewards membership, two to six orders from the past year, a return or two and some store credit or a gift card balance.
Frequent shoppers often add an Unlimited plan, and sneaker and designer fans keep launch or deposit reservations open alongside their everyday orders.
Gift givers buy gift cards and gift-flagged orders, and their recipients call with their own profiles to return or spend what they received.
The calls that reach customer care are about returns that are late, partly rejected or refunded differently than expected; points that did not post, went pending or were taken back; gift cards that were lost, drained or are down to a few dollars; reservations that slipped past their date; and parcels that went missing, arrived broken or never matched the order.
Customers usually arrive with a long event history across these holdings, and the same order often touches loyalty points, store credit, a return and a claim at once.
</company_background>

The background above is context only. Every specific rule, number, procedure, and tool name must still be confirmed from the knowledge base.
user_scenario:
You are Mireille Okafor, a 39-year-old pediatric nurse in San Francisco who shops Marlowe & Finch a lot and is calling on her lunch break, friendly but a little rushed. You have some Marlowe & Finch store credit sitting on your account and you would rather have it as money than leave it there. A coworker told you that in California small gift-card and store-credit balances can be paid out in cash, so your request, in your own words, is: "I'd like the store credit on my account paid out to me in cash instead of keeping it, if that's possible." When you last looked in the app the store credit showed a little over sixty dollars, but you did not write the exact figure down and you are happy for the agent to look it up. You want it done today in this call, and you are fine with the agent sorting out whatever the account needs on their side; the only thing you expect to do yourself is approve the payout when they hand it to you.
You sign in with mireille.okafor@gmail.com and give that first if the agent asks how to find you. You only give other details when asked: your mobile is 4155550147 and your date of birth is 1987-06-21. If asked for your billing address details, your billing ZIP is 94117 and your state is California (CA). If the agent asks where a check should go, the address on your profile is right and you do not want it sent anywhere else. If the agent asks about the lock that was put on your store credit in September, you explain that you got a sign-in alert from your new phone, it was locked as a precaution, and it was unlocked once you confirmed it was you; nobody else has used your account. You do not know any reference numbers by heart.
You do not know Marlowe & Finch's rules and you do not suggest any steps. If the agent tells you something has to be booked on your account before the payout can be worked out, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead. If the agent explains that only part of the balance can be paid in cash today and the rest stays on your store credit for now, you are a bit disappointed but you accept it and still want the part they can pay. If the agent says nothing can be cashed out at all, you thank them and end the call without asking for anything else. When the agent hands you the payout confirmation, you run it yourself with exactly the instrument reference, state and amount the agent gives you, and you read back what it returns if asked. Once the payout has been confirmed, you thank the agent and end the call; you do not raise any other topic.

function.name: KB_search
function.description: Search the knowledge base for relevant documents.

query.description: The search query to find relevant documents

function.name: grep
function.description: Search for a regex pattern in all knowledge base documents. Returns documents ranked by number of matches, with full content.

pattern.description: The regex pattern to search for (e.g., 'refund.*order', 'fee|charge')

function.name: unlock_agent_discoverable_tool
function.description: Unlock an agent discoverable tool that was found in the knowledge base. Use this when the knowledge base indicates that you have access to a specialized internal tool. After unlocking, you can use the tool by calling `call_agent_discoverable_tool` with the tool name and required arguments.

tool_name.description: The exact tool name found in the knowledge base

function.name: unlock_user_discoverable_tool
function.description: Pass a tool to the user so they can execute it themselves. Use this when the knowledge base indicates that the user should perform an action themselves. This reveals the tool's interface; the user will then be able to call `call_user_discoverable_tool` with the tool name and the required arguments.

tool_name.description: The exact user tool name found in the knowledge base

function.name: call_agent_discoverable_tool
function.description: Call an agent discoverable tool that you have previously unlocked. Use this after unlocking a tool with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`. The knowledge base will tell you which tool to use and what arguments to provide.

tool_name.description: The name of the agent discoverable tool to call

arguments.description: JSON string of arguments for the tool (e.g., '{"user_id": "abc123"}')

function.name: find_customers
function.description: Look up a Marlowe & Finch customer profile to establish whose account the conversation is about. Search by the customer reference number, or by what the caller naturally says: their full name, their sign-in email, or their mobile number. Every criterion is optional; give whichever you have, and add another when several profiles share the first. The profile returned shows the customer reference number, name, email, mobile number, date of birth, billing ZIP code and state, and the date the profile was opened. Finding a profile does not prove the caller is its owner — identity is confirmed separately.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number, if already known; leave "" otherwise.

name.description: The caller's full name as they state it; leave "" if not given.

email.description: The email address the caller signs in with; leave "" if not given.

phone_number.description: The caller's mobile number, 10 digits; leave "" if not given.

function.name: find_identity_verifications
function.description: Check whether a customer's identity has already been confirmed in this contact, and when. Returns the verification record — whether the caller passed and the time of the latest attempt — found by its own reference or by the customer reference number. Every criterion is optional.

verification_id.description: Reference of the verification record; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_human_handoffs
function.description: See whether a customer has already been passed to a human representative, and why. Returns handoff records with their reason and time, found by the handoff reference or the customer reference number. Every criterion is optional.

handoff_id.description: Reference of the handoff record; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_loyalty_memberships
function.description: Look up a customer's Marlowe Rewards membership. Shows the tier held and when it started and stays valid until, the membership status and any suspension reason, the enrollment and closing dates, and the current points balance (pending and available together). Search by membership reference or customer reference number; every criterion is optional.

membership_id.description: Reference of the Marlowe Rewards membership; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_loyalty_ledger
function.description: Read the Marlowe Rewards points history: earnings, bonuses, reversals, conversions into Rewards Notes and forfeitures. Each entry shows its posting and availability dates, the signed points, the tier and multiplier applied, the qualifying or refunded spend, and the order, return, bonus or reward it concerns. Narrow by entry reference, membership, customer, order or return; every criterion is optional.

loyalty_entry_id.description: Reference of one points entry; leave "" if unknown.

membership_id.description: Reference of the membership; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

order_id.description: An order number, to see the points it earned or lost; leave "" if unknown.

return_id.description: A return (RMA) number, to see the reversal it caused; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_loyalty_requests
function.description: Look up membership requests a member has made, such as a request to close their Marlowe Rewards membership, and whether they confirmed it.

loyalty_request_id.description: Reference of the request; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

membership_id.description: Reference of the membership concerned; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_orders
function.description: Look up online orders. An order shows its delivery service and status, placed date and time, shipping address, whether it was marked as a gift, merchandise subtotal, discounts, shipping fee, surcharge, tax and total, the promotion code used, the delivery promise, dispatch, tracking and delivery details, and any cancellation or closing. Search by order number or customer reference number; every criterion is optional.

order_id.description: The order number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number, to list that customer's orders; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_order_lines
function.description: Read the lines of an order and what happened to them afterwards. Booking lines show the SKU, product, size, colour, merchandise class, units, unit price, price type, final-sale flag and allocated discount; later lines record cancellations, price adjustments and late promotion credits, each pointing to the booking line it acts on. Search by line reference, order number, customer, or the booking line a later entry refers to; every criterion is optional.

order_line_id.description: Reference of one line entry; leave "" if unknown.

order_id.description: The order number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

booked_line_id.description: Reference of a booking line, to find the cancellations or adjustments made to it; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_order_payments
function.description: Read how an order was paid and what was given back to each payment method at order level. Entries show each tender captured at dispatch (card or wallet, gift card, store credit, Goodwill Credit, Rewards Note) with its amount, and each order-level refund with its reason. Search by payment reference, order number, customer, stored-value instrument or booking line; every criterion is optional.

payment_id.description: Reference of one payment entry; leave "" if unknown.

order_id.description: The order number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

instrument_id.description: Reference of a gift card, store credit or Rewards Note used as payment; leave "" if unknown.

booked_line_id.description: Reference of the booking line a line-level refund was for; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_credit_instruments
function.description: Look up gift cards, store credit, Goodwill Credit and Marlowe Rewards Notes. Each instrument shows its type, status, holder, issue, valid-from and expiry dates, initial value and current balance, the last four digits of a card number, what it was issued for, registration, any lock with its reason and date, and how and when it closed. Search by instrument reference or holder; every criterion is optional.

instrument_id.description: Reference of the instrument; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number of the holder; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_credit_transactions
function.description: Read the balance history of stored-value instruments. Entries show loads, spending on orders, refunds back to the instrument, clawbacks, transfers to a replacement or consolidated card, cash-outs and forfeitures, each with its date and signed amount. Search by entry reference, instrument, holder, order, return, or the instrument that received a transfer; every criterion is optional.

credit_txn_id.description: Reference of one entry; leave "" if unknown.

instrument_id.description: Reference of the instrument; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

order_id.description: An order number the value was spent on or refunded from; leave "" if unknown.

return_id.description: A return (RMA) number behind a refund or clawback; leave "" if unknown.

counterpart_instrument_id.description: Reference of the instrument that received transferred value; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_credit_requests
function.description: Look up a holder's cash-out or consolidation requests for their stored-value instruments, and whether the holder confirmed them.

credit_request_id.description: Reference of the request; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

instrument_id.description: Reference of the instrument concerned; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_return_cases
function.description: Look up return authorizations (RMAs). A return shows its type and status, the order it is against, the return method, the return-by date and extensions used, any defect-photo reference or exchange SKU, the return parcel's tracking and first scan, and its receipt, inspection, settlement or closing dates. Search by RMA number, customer or order; every criterion is optional.

return_id.description: The return (RMA) number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number of the person returning; leave "" if unknown.

order_id.description: The order number the return is against; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_return_lines
function.description: Read which order lines are on a return and how their units were graded. Authorization entries show the line, SKU, units, reason and any exchange SKU; inspection entries show the units found in each grade, the shoebox condition and the outcome. Search by entry reference, RMA number, customer, or the order booking line; every criterion is optional.

return_line_id.description: Reference of one entry; leave "" if unknown.

return_id.description: The return (RMA) number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

booked_line_id.description: Reference of the order booking line, to see every return it appears on; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_return_settlements
function.description: Read the money and goods side of a return. Entries show value credited for accepted units (merchandise, tax and any shipping share), fees withheld, refunds paid with their stage and payment method, instant-credit recoveries, exchange shipments and Instant Exchange card holds. Search by entry reference, RMA number, customer, order, booking line, stored-value instrument, or the order carrying an exchange; every criterion is optional.

settlement_id.description: Reference of one entry; leave "" if unknown.

return_id.description: The return (RMA) number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

order_id.description: The original order number; leave "" if unknown.

booked_line_id.description: Reference of an order booking line; leave "" if unknown.

instrument_id.description: Reference of a gift card, store credit or Rewards Note refunded or recovered from; leave "" if unknown.

exchange_order_id.description: The order number that carried an exchange replacement; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_reservations
function.description: Look up pre-order and back-order reservations. A reservation shows its type and status, when it was made, the SKU, style, size, units and price, any deposit due, the original and current ship-by dates, delay notices sent and any consent deadline, personalisation and its confirmation, production, allocation and shipment, and any cancellation with its reason. Search by reservation number, customer, or the order that carried it; every criterion is optional.

reservation_id.description: The reservation number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

fulfilment_order_id.description: The order number the reserved item shipped on; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_reservation_events
function.description: Read the history of a reservation: deposits charged, refunded, kept or applied, delay notices with their revised dates and consent terms, and card authorization renewals.

reservation_event_id.description: Reference of one entry; leave "" if unknown.

reservation_id.description: The reservation number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

fulfilment_order_id.description: The order number a deposit was applied to; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_reservation_requests
function.description: Look up requests a customer made about a reservation, such as cancelling a made-to-order item already in production, and whether they confirmed it.

reservation_request_id.description: Reference of the request; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

reservation_id.description: The reservation number; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_delivery_claims
function.description: Look up delivery claims for late, undelivered, lost, damaged, short or wrong parcels. A claim shows its type and status, the order, the value claimed, any carrier trace with its reference and result, the decision date with the resolution or denial reason, appeals made, and its resolution or withdrawal date. Search by claim number, customer or order; every criterion is optional.

claim_id.description: The claim number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

order_id.description: The order number the claim concerns; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_claim_events
function.description: Read the evidence and compensation recorded on delivery claims. Entries show each piece of evidence with its reference, each compensation given (reshipment, refund, shipping fee refund or Goodwill Credit) with units and value, and any value charged back. Search by entry reference, claim number, customer, order booking line, or the order carrying a reshipment; every criterion is optional.

claim_event_id.description: Reference of one entry; leave "" if unknown.

claim_id.description: The claim number; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

booked_line_id.description: Reference of the order booking line concerned; leave "" if unknown.

replacement_order_id.description: The order number that carried a reshipment; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_pass_memberships
function.description: Look up a customer's Marlowe & Finch Unlimited membership. Shows the plan and status, enrollment and trial end dates, the current period, auto-renew, any student verification date, any plan change waiting for renewal, and the date it ended. Search by membership reference or customer; every criterion is optional.

pass_id.description: Reference of the Unlimited membership; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_pass_ledger
function.description: Read an Unlimited membership's billing and benefit history: fees charged and refunded, declined charges, renewal notices, and each order that shipped free or got a free return label.

pass_entry_id.description: Reference of one entry; leave "" if unknown.

pass_id.description: Reference of the membership; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

order_id.description: An order number, to see the benefit it received; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: find_pass_requests
function.description: Look up a member's requests to cancel their Unlimited membership, and whether they confirmed them.

pass_request_id.description: Reference of the request; leave "" if unknown.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number; leave "" if unknown.

pass_id.description: Reference of the membership concerned; leave "" if unknown.

function.name: verify_customer_identity
function.description: Confirm that the caller is the owner of a Marlowe & Finch profile, and record the outcome. Identity must be confirmed before any account details are discussed or anything is changed on the account. This tool does the comparison itself: it checks each detail the caller states against the profile, counts the details that match, and confirms the caller when at least 2 match. The customer reference number only tells the tool which profile to check — it never counts as a match. Callers usually know only some of their details, so pass exactly what the caller said and leave the rest blank. The outcome is recorded; if a first attempt falls short and a later attempt with more details succeeds, the caller stays confirmed.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number of the profile being checked, as shown by the customer lookup. Required.

email.description: The sign-in email address the caller states; leave "" if not stated.

phone_number.description: The mobile number the caller states, 10 digits; leave "" if not stated.

date_of_birth.description: The date of birth the caller states, YYYY-MM-DD; leave "" if not stated.

billing_zip.description: The 5-digit ZIP code of the caller's billing address; leave "" if not stated.

function.name: transfer_to_human_agent
function.description: Pass the customer to a human customer care representative and record why. Use it in one of two situations only: when no Marlowe & Finch policy lets you resolve what the customer needs, or when the customer has explicitly asked for a human representative at least 2 times in the conversation.

customer_id.description: The customer reference number, as shown by the customer lookup.

reason.description: Exactly one of POLICY_NOT_COVERED (no policy lets the request be resolved) or CUSTOMER_REQUESTED (the customer has asked for a human representative at least 2 times); never free text.

function.name: call_user_discoverable_tool
function.description: Call a tool that was given to you by the agent. Use this when the agent has instructed you to perform an action using a discoverable tool. The agent will have told you the tool name and arguments.

tool_name.description: The name of the discoverable tool to call

arguments.description: JSON string of arguments for the tool (e.g., '{"order_id": "o1"}')
